rulings.challenge_claim: The rival is dismissed by denying an addressee shift that the cited verse's own bytes name explicitly, and the second divine frame inside the span is never quoted or attributed.
rulings.grounds: Verified in the row's favour first: the three parashah disclosures all check out as SAMEKH at MT 37:38 (front seam), MT 38:3 (interior) and MT 38:8 (own close), correctly typed, single-witness, and correctly held as tier-3 corroboration rather than as the reason for keeping the healing episode together; no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere inside MT 38:1-38:8 (the zone's notes are at MT 36:12, 37:30 and 39:2); and the opening divine frame is correctly owned. (1) UPHELD. The rival sentence dismisses a cut at 38:4 as coming 'with no addressee or scene shift of its own'. MT 38:4 reads וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.38.4, byte): the addressee is named in the verse's own bytes and is the PROPHET, where the first word was delivered to the king - MT 38:1 carries וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו (oshb:Isa.38.1, byte) - and MT 38:5 then commissions a fresh address, הָל֞וֹךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ (oshb:Isa.38.5, byte). An explicitly named addressee change is tier-1, so the warrant denies a signal the bytes carry. Held in proportion, and this is why low is the right register: the rejection has TWO conjuncts, and the first - that the second word answers the first inside one continuous healing episode - is sound and carries the rejection on its own. The false conjunct is an over-claim appended to a good ground, not a bad ground. The bound is untouched. (2) UPHELD. MT 38:5 carries a second divine koh-amar with a DIFFERENT title stack, כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔יךָ (oshb:Isa.38.5, byte), against the bare frame of MT 38:1. The row rests its whole front edge on frame ownership yet leaves this interior frame unquoted and its owner unnamed - in the one zone of the book where the same formula is also used by named human speakers (4 royal-messenger verses at MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3 against 44 divine-frame verses). A frame-ownership row owes the interior frame the same naming it gives the onset. (3) UPHELD, with the challenge's own wording CORRECTED. MT 38:7 opens וְזֶה לְּךָ֥ הָא֖וֹת (oshb:Isa.38.7, byte) and MT 37:30 opens וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.37.30, byte). The challenge calls these 'byte-shared'; they are NOT. The accents differ on two of the three tokens, so the pair is byte-distinct and matches only at finals-normalized SKELETON tier, at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses) - which is how the challenge's own tier citation reads, so the defect is its evidence prose, not its finding. The second link is exact as stated: MT 38:6's וְגַנּוֹתִ֖י עַל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּֽאת (oshb:Isa.38.6, byte) is the second of that clause's two book-wide sites, the first being MT 37:35's וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את (oshb:Isa.37.35, byte; sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). Both links are undisclosed, and both cross this row's own front seam.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: strike the byte-false conjunct 'with no addressee or scene shift of its own' and keep the sound ground (the second word answers the first inside one continuous healing episode); if the addressee question is engaged at all, it must be engaged as a real tier-1 signal that the continuous-episode reading outweighs, not denied. One sentence, plus at most a second carrying the rival disclosure. boundary_rationale: splice the interior divine frame at oshb:Isa.38.5 with its tier and NAME its owner, as the row already does for the onset frame at oshb:Isa.38.1, and note its distinct title stack; frame ownership must be named at every counted site in this zone, not only at the row's edges. device_notes: disclose both cross-seam device links with their correct tiers - the sign-formula pair at oshb:Isa.37.30 and oshb:Isa.38.7 (sweep: 2 verses, finals-normalized SKELETON tier, NOT byte-identical) and the defend-this-city clause at oshb:Isa.37.35 and oshb:Isa.38.6 (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier) - under cross-seam cohesion. boundary_evidence_refs: mirror oshb:Isa.37.30 and oshb:Isa.37.35 once they are argued in prose. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the addressee/frame-ownership check that killed the original - MT 38:4's named addressee must not be denied, every koh-amar site inside the span must carry a named owner, and each cross-seam device must carry a tier the collator actually returns (skeleton, not byte, for both pairs).

rulings.challenge_claim: The three-site Yah digit is attached to a swept object the sweep does not return, and the rear edge is asserted in English while two divine-title sites inside the span and a seam-straddling adjacency go unengaged.
rulings.grounds: The bound is correct and gate-ratified - the mikhtav header and the psalm it heads are ONE hymn_doxology unit - and nothing here moves it. Verified in the row's favour: the header-class distinction is byte-supported, מִכְתָּ֖ב לְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.38.9, byte) being a psalm-type writing-superscription and not a chazah/ben-Amots frame; no parashah mark and no ketiv/qere note falls inside MT 38:9-38:20; and the preceding SAMEKH at MT 38:8 is correctly typed and disclosed. (1) UPHELD - a count-object defect, not an arithmetic one. The row calls MT 38:11's doubled יָ֔הּ יָ֖הּ (oshb:Isa.38.11, byte) 'one of only three standalone-Yah sites in the book', and device_notes repeats it with a digit attached, 'exactly three standalone-Yah sites book-wide (sweep: 3 sites)'. The 3-verse digit belongs to the standalone-OR-PREFIXED short-form object. A finals-normalized EXACT-TOKEN sweep of the standalone short form returns TWO verses: MT 12:2 יָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה and MT 38:11 יָ֔הּ יָ֖הּ (byte tier). The third site carries the PREFIXED form, MT 26:4 בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.26.4, byte), and is therefore outside the object the row names. 'The only doubled one' is byte-true and survives. Two further wording faults ride along: the citation says 'sweep: 3 sites' without naming its unit, where the sanctioned shorthand names verses. (2) UPHELD. The rear seam is argued only as 'Hezekiah's own vow of temple song'. Its byte warrant - the third-person wayyiqtol onset וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.38.21, byte) against the psalm's first person - is never quoted, and a byte-true adjacency straddles that seam undisclosed: בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה closes MT 38:20 and the same two tokens stand at the close of MT 38:22 (byte tier; sweep: 6 verses book-wide at finals-normalized skeleton tier, 4 at byte). (3) UPHELD, and it is the sharpest of the four. The bare-adonai token stands TWICE inside the span - אֲדֹנָ֖י at MT 38:14 and אֲדֹנָ֖י at MT 38:16 (byte tier), both qamats-pointed, i.e. the divine side of the census that is role-split in exactly this zone - and the row itself OPENS the divine-name object with its Yah disclosure and then leaves these two unengaged. Symmetry is a sweep, not a spot fix; having elected the object, the row owes it across the whole span. (4) UPHELD. device_notes justifies the bounding by appeal to a governance ruling ('This bounding follows the owner ruling that...'). That is an evidentiary misplacement at minimum - a header-bounded hymn claim belongs on the bytes - and it sits squarely in the register class barring governance and review-actor narration from row prose. The ruling remains binding; it simply may not be the row's stated warrant. WHERE THE CHALLENGE UNDER-RATES (the refinement): severity. The challenge sets low. Two of these four are law-level rather than cosmetic - a digit citation attached to a misnamed object inside the named divine-name count-object hazard class, and a governance appeal standing in row prose as the stated warrant - and a third is a symmetry miss on the object the row itself elected. Corrected finding: same four defects, severity MEDIUM. That the Yah note is disclosed as texture rather than as a boundary driver limits the blast radius but does not exempt it from the count discipline, which is not scaled by boundary-relevance.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale and device_notes: re-name the count-object. Either cite the 3-verse digit against the standalone-OR-PREFIXED short-form object, or cite the standalone object with its true digit (sweep: 2 verses, MT 12:2 and MT 38:11), noting that MT 26:4 carries the prefixed form. Keep 'the only doubled one', which is byte-true. State the unit in the shorthand (verses, not 'sites'). boundary_rationale: splice the rear-seam byte warrant - the third-person wayyiqtol onset at oshb:Isa.38.21 against the psalm's first-person voice - and mirror oshb:Isa.38.21 in boundary_evidence_refs once argued. device_notes: disclose the temple-house adjacency straddling the rear seam (oshb:Isa.38.20 and oshb:Isa.38.22) with its tier and digit, under cross-seam cohesion. device_notes: complete symmetry on the divine-name object the row itself opened - disclose the two qamats-pointed bare-adonai tokens at oshb:Isa.38.14 and oshb:Isa.38.16 as the divine side of the census that is role-split in this zone. device_notes: replace the governance-ruling appeal with the byte warrant for the bound - the mikhtav header class at oshb:Isa.38.9, the first-person psalm run it governs, and the third-person onset that closes it at oshb:Isa.38.21. The bound itself does NOT change. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the divine-name count-object sweep that killed the original - the standalone short-form sweep must return 2 verses and the standalone-or-prefixed object 3, with the row's digit matching whichever object it names; every bare-adonai site inside MT 38:9-38:20 must be disclosed; and no field may carry a governance ruling as the stated warrant.

rulings.challenge_claim: The two-verse isolation is argued as an English register shift while the byte-true links that straddle its own front seam, and the sign account its placement argument depends on, are neither quoted nor cited.
rulings.grounds: The challenge's first and headline item is REFUTED by the row's own bytes; its other two stand. (1) REFUTED. The challenge says 'the person-shift ground is byte-true but unquoted ... so the row's only positive boundary warrant stands as an English register observation'. The row quotes BOTH verses in full, pointed, each labelled tier: byte, and each quoted run OPENS with the third-person wayyiqtol the ground depends on: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ heads the spliced run at oshb:Isa.38.21 and וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ heads the spliced run at oshb:Isa.38.22. The refuting bytes are the row's own quotations. The engagement-class rule - pointed splices plus tier labels for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim - is satisfied here, not breached. What is genuinely missing is far smaller and must be stated as such: the row does not NAME the form class inside the run, and the FIRST-person side of its own contrast (MT 38:20) is carried in English only, that verse lying outside this span. (2) UPHELD as an obligation, REFINED as to force. בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה closes MT 38:20 and the byte-identical two tokens close MT 38:22 (byte tier), so a device does straddle this row's front seam undisclosed and disclosure is owed under cross-seam cohesion. But its evidential force is low and the challenge overstates it as arguing continuity with the preceding unit: the same two tokens are byte-identical at 4 verses book-wide and THREE of those sit inside this one episode - MT 37:1 וַיָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה, MT 38:20 and MT 38:22 (sweep: 4 verses byte, 6 at finals-normalized skeleton tier) - so it is an episode-wide temple motif that straddles every seam in chs 37-38 alike, and argues no more against this seam than against any other. Disclose it; do not weight it. (3) UPHELD. The placement argument turns on these verses standing 'after rather than before the healing narrative's own sign account', yet no verse of that sign account is named or cited anywhere in the row, and boundary_evidence_refs carries none of them. The chain is byte-recoverable and short: וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת at MT 37:30 and וְזֶה לְּךָ֥ הָא֖וֹת at MT 38:7 (sweep: 2 verses, finals-normalized skeleton tier) feeding this span's bare א֑וֹת at MT 38:22 (sweep: 5 verses book-wide for the unprefixed token). A row whose held-open placement question IS its main claim owes those verses a citation. Verified in the row's favour: the SAMEKH at MT 38:22 is correctly typed and single-witness-disclosed; no ketiv/qere note falls in the span; the medium_low hold and the frontier flag are appropriate to a genuinely open placement question; and the synoptic parallel is correctly confined to prose as typed-relation metadata, kept out of boundary_evidence_refs, with the verses never rearranged to match it - exactly as the zone requires.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: name the form class inside the two runs already spliced (third-person wayyiqtol onsets at oshb:Isa.38.21 and oshb:Isa.38.22) so the person-shift ground reads off the bytes it already carries, and mark the first-person side of the contrast at web:Isa.38.20 as the English rendering of an out-of-span verse. No new splice is required for the third-person side; it is already there. device_notes: disclose the temple-house adjacency across the row's front seam (oshb:Isa.38.20 and oshb:Isa.38.22) with its tier and digit, and state its weight honestly as an episode-wide motif rather than a seam-specific tie. boundary_rationale and boundary_evidence_refs: NAME and MIRROR the sign-account verses the placement argument depends on - oshb:Isa.38.7 within the healing narrative and oshb:Isa.37.30 in the preceding episode - with the sign-formula pair tier-labelled (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier) and the bare sign noun at oshb:Isa.38.22 given its own digit and object. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the out-of-span reference mirror that the placement claim currently evades - every verse the placement argument leans on must be named in prose AND present in boundary_evidence_refs, and every cross-seam device must carry its tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: The mandated rival is described in terms the cited verse's bytes contradict - as worded it restates the row's own bound rather than an alternative - and the rear-edge frame claim carries no quoted frame form.
rulings.grounds: All four items confirmed from bytes, and a fifth defect neither primary raised is recorded below. (1) UPHELD. The rival proposes 'extending this unit through Isaiah's own questioning at web:Isa.39.5'. MT 39:5 carries no interrogative whatever: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.39.5, byte) - a summons, whose three-token frame שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת is the SOLE site of that formula in the book (sweep: 1 verse, byte and finals-normalized skeleton alike). The prophet's questioning stands at MT 39:3, מָ֥ה אָמְר֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וּמֵאַ֨יִן֙ יָבֹ֣אוּ, and at MT 39:4, וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֥ה רָא֖וּ בְּבֵיתֶ֑ךָ (byte tier) - both INSIDE this row's own span. So as worded the rival names the row's existing bound rather than an alternative to it, and the same sentence then attributes a herald-summons to that same verse, contradicting its own label. Read charitably the INTENT is a genuine rival - a cut after MT 39:5 rather than after MT 39:4 - which is why the cure is a re-wording and not the invention of a new rival; but this is the mandated rival field, and a field whose two halves label one verse incompatibly cannot stand. (2) UPHELD. The rear-edge warrant is a frame-based seam claim - the following unit is 'introduced by a fresh herald-summons' - with no frame form quoted anywhere in the row. The form exists, is short, and is unique in the book, so the omission is not a shortage of evidence. (3) UPHELD, minor. The ketiv/qere at MT 39:2 is correctly disclosed against the inventory's single note there, but the row does not name which of the two staged forms its treasury gloss follows; the pair stands as נכתה נְכֹת֡וֹ in the verse bytes (oshb:Isa.39.2, byte), the first form unpointed. A row that slices a K/Q verse names the forms. (4) UPHELD. The oracle takes Hezekiah's own wording back up across the row's rear edge: כָּל אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּבֵיתִי֙ at MT 39:4 against כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵיתֶ֗ךָ at MT 39:6 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, finals-normalized skeleton tier), with the treasury chain running MT 39:2 בְּאֹֽצְרֹתָ֑יו - DEFECTIVE - MT 39:4 בְּאוֹצְרֹתָֽי - PLENE - and MT 39:6 אָצְר֧וּ (byte tier). A plene/defective pair two verses apart inside one chain is the mater-lectionis hazard class in miniature; note for the author that a raw consonantal sweep of that root BLENDS a second root and must not be cited as a treasury digit - name the three attested sites instead. NEW FINDING (raised by neither primary): device_notes asserts that 'the embassy's own display-of-treasury motif closes without remainder before Isaiah's separate judgment word begins.' That is an AFFIRMATIVE claim the bytes contradict, not merely an undisclosed link: the motif demonstrably does NOT close without remainder, since both the possession-catchword and the treasury root are reactivated at MT 39:6, one verse into the following unit. The distinction matters for the cure - an omission is repaired by adding a disclosure, a false closure claim must be struck.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: re-word so the rival names what it actually proposes - carrying the unit through MT 39:5, the prophet's summons - and stop calling MT 39:5 'Isaiah's own questioning', which the bytes place at MT 39:3 and MT 39:4, inside the span. One sentence, plus at most a second carrying the rival disclosure. The bound does not change. boundary_rationale: splice the herald-summons frame at oshb:Isa.39.5 with its tier and its digit (sweep: 1 verse book-wide), since the rear-edge seam claim rests on that form; oshb:Isa.39.5 is already mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs. device_notes: name which of the two staged forms at oshb:Isa.39.2 the treasury gloss follows (ketiv unpointed, qere pointed), since the row reads a gloss out of that verse. device_notes (NEW FINDING cure): STRIKE 'closes without remainder' - it is byte-false - and replace it with the disclosed cross-seam link: the possession catchword at oshb:Isa.39.4 taken back up at oshb:Isa.39.6 (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier) and the treasury chain across oshb:Isa.39.2, oshb:Isa.39.4 and oshb:Isa.39.6, with the defective and plene spellings named per attested spelling and NO blended root digit cited. Mirror oshb:Isa.39.6 in boundary_evidence_refs. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the checks that killed the original - MT 39:5 must not be described as carrying a question; the rival must name a bound different from the row's own; the rear-edge frame form must be spliced and tier-labelled; and no field may claim the treasury motif closes without remainder while the catchword and the root recur at MT 39:6.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's only rear-edge warrant carries an explicit byte-tier label with nothing collated behind it, and the postpositive contrast blends two distinct censuses without a digit, a named object or a quoted form.
rulings.grounds: Verified in the row's favour first, and it is a substantial list: the frame parent and the frame seam at MT 39:8 | MT 40:1 are handled correctly and the row does not straddle it; the petuchah at MT 39:8 and the setumah at MT 40:2 are correctly typed and never conflated; chs 39-40 are identity numbering so no dual or numeric qualifier is owed; no ketiv/qere note falls in the span; both WEB runs are verbatim; and the attribution of the plural comforters is honestly held open rather than assigned - which is right, since the herald-voice attribution across MT 40:1-11 is a question a chunking row never decides. Nothing below touches it. (1) UPHELD, and it is the cleanest defect of the five rows. The rejected-alternative sentence cites oshb:Isa.40.3 with an explicit 'tier: byte' label and quotes no Hebrew at all - a tier asserted with nothing collated behind it, which is the tier-disclosure standard breached at its plainest. The form the argument needs was available and is two tokens long: MT 40:3 opens ק֣וֹל קוֹרֵ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.3, byte), the sole site of that herald onset in the book (sweep: 1 verse, byte and finals-normalized skeleton alike). (2) UPHELD. 'the tetragrammaton signature used in most of the book's postpositive formulas' carries no digit, names no swept object, and blends two censuses that must stay apart: the postpositive oracle signature (23 verses book-wide, whose only narrative-zone site is MT 37:34's נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, byte tier) and the amar-plus-tetragrammaton adjacency (52 verses). The row's own inquit, יֹאמַ֖ר אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1, byte), is the Elohim variant and is excluded from the adjacency census outright - which is the fact the contrast actually needs and the one it never states. No contrast form is quoted, so a comparison the row makes its onset argument out of stands on English alone, and 'most' is a quantifier with no digit behind it. (3) UPHELD. The PLURAL number of the imperatives is the hinge of the unnamed-comforters reading and is never named: נַחֲמ֥וּ נַחֲמ֖וּ at MT 40:1 and דַּבְּר֞וּ with וְקִרְא֣וּ at MT 40:2 (byte tier) are spliced but described only as 'a doubled imperative command' and as 'addressed to unnamed comforters'. With no morphology layer staged, the plural is nonetheless carried in the letter bytes and in both witnesses' renderings, so it is a byte-checkable claim the row leaves unstated while resting an argument on it. NEW FINDING (raised by neither primary): device_notes grounds its unit_type handling in a governance allowance - 'per the operative-category allowance for the closed unit_type vocabulary'. That is the same register class the challenge flags in the sibling hymn row of this cluster, and it is unflagged here, so it is also an internal asymmetry across the pair: a governance rule may govern the row, but it may not stand in row prose as the row's stated warrant.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: splice the herald onset at oshb:Isa.40.3 and let the existing tier label rest on collated bytes; add its digit (sweep: 1 verse book-wide). The sentence must name the FORM only - the rival is a fresh voice-onset - and must NOT assign the speaker, since the herald-voice attribution stays open. One sentence, plus at most a second carrying the rival disclosure. boundary_rationale: re-cut the postpositive contrast so it names ONE object and carries a digit. State that the row's inquit is the Elohim variant, excluded from the amar-plus-tetragrammaton adjacency census (52 verses), and keep the postpositive oracle-signature census (23 verses) separate; quote the contrast form if the contrast is retained. Delete the undigited 'most'. boundary_rationale or device_notes: name the plural number of the imperatives at oshb:Isa.40.1 and oshb:Isa.40.2 as a byte-checkable form claim, since the plural addressee is what the unnamed-comforters reading rests on - naming the FORM only, never the referent, which stays held open. device_notes (NEW FINDING cure): replace the governance-allowance appeal with the substantive ground for the unit_type call, argued from the bytes of the onset. The vocabulary rule remains binding; it may not be the row's stated warrant. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the tier and count-object checks that killed the original - every 'tier: byte' label in the row must have a collated pointed run behind it; the postpositive comparison must name a single swept object with a digit and must not blend the 23-verse signature census with the 52-verse adjacency census; and no field may cite a governance allowance as the row's warrant.
